answer: Ridge-Weighted Fee Escalation. Each new identity pays a base fee that scales with a ridge function of how many identities already share its network fingerprint (IP subnet, timing, funding source). Fees rise steeply along that ridge, not as a flat gate. The wharf effect: identities must stay active and transact to avoid decay, so dormant clones cost upkeep. An anchor deposit covers one identity only and is forfeited if the fingerprint cluster grows past a threshold.
